issue.title: Add Source Code Text Parser Module

labels.name: module:text
labels.description: Issues related to the text module

issue.body: While reading about [Anthony's work](https://www.peruma.me/publication/2022-rit-identifier_names/), I stumbled across [srcML](https://www.srcml.org/#home). This super simple-to-use binary offer means to scan any source code folder, file, etc, to annotate it with tags. This enables parsing any unit within files, hence opening many opportunities to perform text mining on source code.

milestone.title: Milestone 2. Bugzilla Wrapper/Crawler (February 9th-March 14th)
milestone.description:
Bugzilla Wrapper: 

2.1 Implement the BugZilla functionality (via Perceval)
2.2-Create unit tests to test the functionality
2.3-Prepare mid-semester presentation showing deliverables

Bugzilla Crawler:

2.4-Implement the BugZilla crawler
2.5-Create unit tests to test this functionality
2.6-Create vignette demonstrating use of BugZilla wrapper

issue.body:
### Proposal

We will implement a Bugzilla crawler that will be directly called from R. Bugzilla has a REST API, so we can parse the JSON that is returned by the API call in the R function.

The main contributions for this issue will be the Bugzilla crawler functions, unit tests for these functions, and a vignette demonstrating how to use the Bugzilla crawler.

### Architecture

NOTE: We should discuss the architecture of the Bugzilla crawler before starting any code.

As stated by Carlos:
The issues raised on issue #70 of PERCEIVE provide good motivation on why we should refine the requirements of it upfront: https://github.com/sailuh/perceive/issues/70. 

More specifically, we will want to break the Bugzila crawler into a 
- i) "downloader as-is" (which I believe the raw data is json)
- ii) parser of said json into tables. 

The downloader would be under R/download.R, where as the crawler under R/parser.R. 

### Tasks

Deadline Sunday

Leilani:
Pull Request: https://github.com/sailuh/kaiaulu/pull/177
- [x] Bugzilla crawler download function

Malia:

- [x] Bugzilla crawler parse function

Nico:

- [ ] Bugzilla crawler unit tests

Everyone:

- [x] Add Bugzilla Crawler functions and details to Bugzilla vignette

issue.title: Networks in Kaiaulu and 3rd party dependencies

labels.name: priority:future
labels.description: For issues which will be deferred / wishlist

labels.name: module:graph
labels.description: Issues related to the graph module

issue.body:
Currently, Kaiaulu has a really ad-hoc implementation of [networks](https://github.com/sailuh/kaiaulu/blob/master/R/network.R) (i.e. it represents in a list nodes and edges tables, each being a data.table). The definition grew organically to use the visualizations provided by vizNetwork for exploration early on, but it doesn't make sense to, from here onwards, re-code an entire network library. 

In Codeface4Smells, the Smells were built on top of igraph and leverages its bipartite projection algorithms. However, doing so here would automatically re-license the codebase from MPL 2.0 to GPL. Moreover, it is hard to believe igraph is the only library available out there.

This issue is a small survey of existing tools found "in the wild" for consideration, not only based on the license but on features, etc, and for reflection on how far we need to go in regards to dependencies. Generally, I would prefer to not consider such a core data model and functionality of the package dependent on anything (unless it is incorporated directly to the codebase and doesn't cost setup overhead).

issue.title: Perceval version 0.21.2-rc.4 returns error on parse_mbox(), perceval_parsed is empty in Social Smells Notebook

labels.name: module:parser
labels.description: Anything associated to the parser module.

issue.body:
## Problem:
While running social_smell_showcase.Rmd on the Apache Thrift github repository (https://github.com/apache/thrift), on line 139

https://github.com/sailuh/kaiaulu/blob/f66bc0f964861b8c928cda01c6b4b493414bf13a/vignettes/social_smell_showcase.Rmd#L139

I got the following error:

Error in data.table::setnames(perceval_parsed, "data.body", "reply_body") : 
  Items of 'old' not found in column names: [data.body]. Consider skip_absent=TRUE.

### Steps I took to try and fix it:
-Checked my perceval_path and mbox_path and made sure they were correct and relative to my working directory
-Checked my perceval installation & tried different installation methods
-Used a different mbox file. First I tried the one provided for the Apache Thrift project by Rick. Then, I used the mbox here https://lists.apache.org/list.html?dev@thrift.apache.org.
-Tried running the notebook on another project. In particular, I tried to run the notebook for the Apache Helix github repo (https://github.com/apache/helix), but that didn't seem to make a difference. 

### My findings:
I looked at the source of the parse_mbox() function in parser.R, and I tried to learn more about the error.

https://github.com/sailuh/kaiaulu/blob/f66bc0f964861b8c928cda01c6b4b493414bf13a/R/parser.R#L243-L281)

One thing I noticed was that if I set stderr=TRUE in line 250-253 of this function

  perceval_output <- system2(perceval_path,
                             args = c('mbox',mbox_uri,mbox_path,'--json-line'),
                             stdout = TRUE,
                             stderr = TRUE) # set to true

Then I get the following error message:

Error: parse error: after array element, I expect ',' or ']'
                                 [2023-01-26 22:19:07,492] - Sir Perce
                     (right here) ------^

I know the "[2023-01-26 22:19:07,492]" seems to refer to the time I ran the notebook. I believe "Sir Perce" refers to perceval, but I don't understand why perceval is giving this error.

Also if I set verbose=TRUE in line 255 of this function:

line 255)   perceval_parsed <- data.table(jsonlite::stream_in(textConnection(perceval_output),verbose=TRUE)) # changed verbose to TRUE

The console output says "Imported 0 records.  Simplifying...".

So perceval_parsed is an empty table, which I believe explains why I was getting this error from before:

Error in data.table::setnames(perceval_parsed, "data.body", "reply_body") : 
  Items of 'old' not found in column names: [data.body]. Consider skip_absent=TRUE.

Referencing this documentation for the setnames() function, https://rdrr.io/rforge/CALIBERdatamanage/man/setnames.html, I see that "old" represents the old columns of the dataframe, and since the dataframe was empty, "old" wasn't found.

The problem I have is I don't understand why perceval_parsed ends up being empty.

### To replicate error:
-clone Kaiaulu and install Kaiaulu package
-clone Apache Thrift repo (https://github.com/apache/thrift)
-set up the project configuration file for thrift.yml following the example here (https://github.com/sailuh/kaiaulu/blob/master/conf/helix.yml). Specifically, I just set up the version control and mailing list section
-Within, social_smell_showcase.Rmd, change tools_path and conf_path (here: https://github.com/sailuh/kaiaulu/blob/f66bc0f964861b8c928cda01c6b4b493414bf13a/vignettes/social_smell_showcase.Rmd#L58-L59)
-run the social smells notebook

issue.body:
* The Perceval Wrapper functions do not allow for the output to be specified. This is too rigid and inconsistent to the Bugzilla crawler. 
 * The downloader returns a character string instead of a json object. Best to be a path, so the parser instead returns the json object. 
 * Linkage between downloader and parser is missing on parameters.

Note: The fixes have already been made and will be pushed soon.
